entities.name: Lithium iron phosphate battery (LFP)
entities.definition: Lithium-ion battery whose cathode is lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4). It offers high thermal stability and long cycle life but lower energy density than nickel-based chemistries.

entities.name: Nickel manganese cobalt battery (NMC)
entities.definition: Lithium-ion battery using a layered nickel-manganese-cobalt oxide cathode; higher energy density and better cold-weather performance than LFP at higher cost.
entities.source: Wikipedia, Lithium nickel manganese cobalt oxide — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium_nickel_manganese_cobalt_oxide

entities.name: Nickel cobalt aluminium battery (NCA)
entities.definition: Lithium-ion chemistry with a LiNiCoAlO2 cathode, known for very high energy density and used in early long-range EV packs.
entities.source: Wikipedia, Lithium nickel cobalt aluminium oxide — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium_nickel_cobalt_aluminium_oxide

entities.name: Lithium manganese iron phosphate battery (LMFP)
entities.definition: LFP variant with manganese doping that raises the operating voltage, delivering roughly 15-20% higher energy density than plain LFP while keeping olivine safety.

entities.name: Sodium-ion battery
entities.definition: Rechargeable battery that shuttles sodium ions instead of lithium. It uses abundant, low-cost materials and performs well in cold weather but has lower energy density.

entities.name: CATL Naxtra sodium-ion battery
entities.name_zh: 宁德时代 Naxtra 钠新电池
entities.definition: CATL's mass-produced sodium-ion EV battery, rated up to 175 Wh/kg with 5C peak charge and over 90% power retention at -40 degrees C; full-scale mass production targeted for end-2026.
entities.source: CATL official news, Super Technology Day / Naxtra Battery — https://www.catl.com/en/news/6401.html

entities.name: Solid-state battery
entities.definition: Battery in which the liquid electrolyte is replaced by a solid electrolyte, promising higher energy density and improved safety. Automotive volumes remain in pilot production as of 2026.

entities.name: Semi-solid-state battery
entities.definition: Intermediate design using a gel or quasi-solid electrolyte with a small liquid fraction. It has already reached limited series production in long-range packs.

entities.name: CATL condensed-matter battery
entities.definition: CATL high-energy cell built around a condensed electrolyte, announced at 350 Wh/kg at the cell level in 2026.
entities.source: CATL official news, Six Major Innovations — https://www.catl.com/en/news/6811.html

entities.name: BYD Blade Battery
entities.definition: BYD's long, thin LFP cell (about 960 mm) designed as a structural pack element. Its nail-penetration test results show no fire or explosion.
entities.source: BYD official, Blade Battery — https://www.byd.com/en/news (see also ResearchInChina CTP/CTB/CTC report)

entities.name: CATL Qilin battery
entities.definition: CATL's third-generation cell-to-pack battery with a system-level energy density of 255 Wh/kg and 72% pack volume utilisation.
entities.source: CATL official news, Six Major Innovations — https://www.catl.com/en/news/6811.html

entities.name: CATL Shenxing superfast charging battery
entities.definition: LFP battery line built for very high charge rates: the first generation supported 4C charging and later generations claim up to 12C peak, giving roughly 10-minute 10-80% charging.
entities.source: CATL official news, Super Technology Day / Naxtra Battery — https://www.catl.com/en/news/6401.html

entities.name: CATL Freevoy dual-power battery
entities.name_zh: 宁德时代骁遥双核电池
entities.definition: Battery that blends LFP and NCM at the particle level, reaching about 230 Wh/kg and supporting pure-electric plus hybrid operation with combined range above 2,000 km.
entities.source: CATL official news, Six Major Innovations — https://www.catl.com/en/news/6811.html

entities.name: Cell-to-pack (CTP)
entities.definition: Pack architecture that removes modules and places cells directly in the pack enclosure, cutting part count by roughly 40% and lifting volume utilisation to 60-70%.
entities.source: Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering, review of CTB battery-structure integration — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/mechanical-engineering/articles/10.3389/fmech.2026.1825484/full

entities.name: Cell-to-body (CTB)
entities.definition: Design in which the battery pack's upper cover replaces the car's floor, making the pack a load-bearing part of the body structure; introduced by BYD in 2022.
entities.source: ResearchInChina, Passenger Car CTP/CTC/CTB Integrated Battery Industry Report — https://www.researchinchina.com/Htmls/Report/2024/73951.html

entities.name: Cell-to-chassis (CTC)
entities.definition: Architecture in which cells are integrated directly into the vehicle chassis or underbody, so the battery enclosure acts as a floor panel or structural member.
entities.source: ResearchInChina, Passenger Car CTP/CTC/CTB Integrated Battery Industry Report — https://www.researchinchina.com/Htmls/Report/2024/73951.html

entities.name: Cell-to-module (CTM)
entities.definition: Conventional pack architecture in which cells are first assembled into modules that are then installed in the pack, offering easier serviceability at lower volume efficiency.
entities.source: Bonnen Battery, EV battery pack designs from modules to body-integrated power — https://www.bonnenbatteries.com/ev-battery-pack-designs-from-modules-to-body-integrated-power

entities.name: 4680 cylindrical cell
entities.definition: Tesla's 46 mm diameter by 80 mm tall tabless cylindrical cell, claimed to deliver about five times the energy and six times the power of the 2170 format.
entities.source: Tesla Battery Day 2020 / Wikipedia, Tesla 4680 — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_4680

entities.name: 21700 cylindrical cell
entities.definition: 21 mm diameter by 70 mm cylindrical lithium-ion cell format widely used in EV and power-tool packs.

entities.name: 18650 cylindrical cell
entities.definition: 18 mm diameter by 65 mm cylindrical cell, the format that scaled early EV and consumer battery packs.

entities.name: Prismatic cell
entities.definition: Rectangular hard-cased cell format that dominates the Chinese EV market because it packages densely and resists swelling.

entities.name: Pouch cell
entities.definition: Cell sealed in a laminated foil pouch; it has high packaging efficiency and low weight but needs external compression for mechanical support.

entities.name: Tabless electrode design
entities.definition: Electrode construction that replaces discrete tabs with a continuous current-collector edge, shortening the current path to cut internal resistance and enable high-power cells.

entities.name: Dry battery electrode process
entities.definition: Solvent-free electrode manufacturing route that avoids large drying ovens, cutting factory energy use and floor space compared with wet slurry coating.
entities.source: Tesla, Battery Day 2020 (dry electrode process) — https://www.tesla.com/

entities.name: Battery management system (BMS)
entities.definition: Electronics that monitor cell voltage and temperature, estimate state of charge and health, balance cells and enforce protection limits.

entities.name: State of charge (SOC)
entities.definition: The remaining energy in a battery expressed as a percentage of its rated capacity; it governs usable range and charge-power limits.

entities.name: State of health (SOH)
entities.definition: Measure of a battery's current capacity and internal resistance relative to new condition. It is a required data point in the EU battery passport and a key input for used-EV valuation.
entities.source: European Commission, Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Art. 77 & Annex XIII (battery passport, mandatory 18 Feb 2027)

entities.name: EU battery passport
entities.definition: Machine-readable digital record required by Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 for EV, LMT and industrial batteries above 2 kWh placed on the EU market from 18 February 2027, accessed by QR code and covering carbon footprint, recycled content, chemistry and state of health.
entities.source: European Commission, Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Art. 77 & Annex XIII (battery passport, mandatory 18 Feb 2027)

entities.name: Silicon-carbon anode
entities.definition: Anode that blends silicon into graphite to raise capacity beyond pure graphite; carbon scaffolding is used to buffer silicon's large volume expansion.

entities.name: Lithium plating
entities.definition: Deposition of metallic lithium on the anode surface instead of intercalation, typically during fast charging at low temperature. It permanently consumes lithium and can seed dendrites.

entities.name: Calendar aging
entities.definition: Capacity fade that occurs with time regardless of cycling, accelerated by high state of charge and high ambient temperature.

entities.name: Thermal runaway
entities.definition: Self-sustaining exothermic chain reaction inside a cell that can propagate to neighbouring cells; the central failure mode that EV battery safety standards target.

entities.name: LFP thermal stability
entities.definition: The strong P-O bonds and olivine structure of LFP raise its decomposition temperature, giving a longer time between failure onset and fire than nickel-rich chemistries.

entities.name: C-rate
entities.definition: Charge or discharge current normalised to battery capacity: 1C empties or fills the pack in one hour, 5C in about twelve minutes.

entities.name: Cobalt-free battery
entities.definition: Cathode design that avoids cobalt, either by using LFP/LMFP or nickel-manganese-only layered oxides, to reduce cost and supply-chain exposure.
entities.source: Wikipedia, Lithium nickel manganese cobalt oxide — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium_nickel_manganese_cobalt_oxide

entities.name: Second-life battery
entities.definition: Repurposing of retired EV packs into stationary storage before recycling, extending service life and lowering the carbon cost per kWh.

entities.name: Black mass
entities.definition: Shredded and separated battery output that concentrates cathode metals; it is the feedstock for hydrometallurgical recovery of nickel, cobalt and lithium.

entities.name: Gravimetric energy density
entities.definition: Energy stored per unit mass, reported in Wh/kg at cell or pack level; the main lever on EV range for a given battery weight.

entities.name: Volumetric energy density
entities.definition: Energy stored per unit volume in Wh/L; it determines how much battery fits into a fixed floor area.

entities.name: GB/T 20234 charging standard
entities.name_zh: 国标 GB/T 20234 充电标准
entities.definition: Chinese national standard for EV charging connectors and interfaces: GB/T 20234.2 covers AC and GB/T 20234.3 covers DC. The 2023 revision extended DC charging up to 1,500 V and 800 A.

entities.name: GB/T AC charging connector
entities.definition: Seven-pin AC connector defined by GB/T 20234.2, used for single- and three-phase AC charging in mainland China.

entities.name: GB/T DC charging connector
entities.definition: Nine-pin DC connector defined by GB/T 20234.3, mechanically incompatible with CCS and CHAdeMO so adapter hardware is required.

entities.name: GB/T 27930 communication protocol
entities.name_zh: 国标 GB/T 27930 通信协议
entities.definition: CAN-based communication protocol (derived from SAE J1939) between an EV and a DC charger in China, corresponding to ISO 15118 in Western standards.

entities.name: GB/T 18487 conductive charging system
entities.name_zh: 国标 GB/T 18487 传导充电系统
entities.definition: Chinese general requirements standard for conductive charging systems, corresponding to IEC 61851 in the international framework.

entities.name: Combined Charging System 1 (CCS1)
entities.name_zh: 北美 CCS1 充电标准
entities.definition: North American DC standard combining the SAE J1772 Type 1 AC connector with two DC pins, supporting up to 350 kW at 1,000 V.

entities.name: Combined Charging System 2 (CCS2)
entities.name_zh: 欧洲 CCS2 充电标准
entities.definition: European DC standard pairing the IEC 62196 Type 2 AC connector with two DC pins, rated to 1,000 V and 500 A and the mandatory plug for EU public DC charging.

entities.name: CHAdeMO
entities.name_zh: 日本 CHAdeMO 快充标准
entities.definition: DC fast charging standard introduced in Japan in 2010 by the CHAdeMO Association; the original 62.5 kW rating was later extended to 200 kW and beyond, and it supports bidirectional V2G.
entities.source: Driivz, EV charging standards and protocols — https://driivz.com/blog/ev-charging-standards-and-protocols

entities.name: North American Charging Standard (NACS)
entities.definition: Tesla-designed charging connector opened to the industry and standardised by SAE: a Technical Information Report was published in December 2023 and the J3400 Recommended Practice in September 2024. Most North American automakers have adopted it for DC fast charging.
entities.source: SAE International, SAE J3400 North American Charging System Recommended Practice / EV Charging Stations news — https://evchargingstations.com/chargingnews/sae-released-its-j3400-nacs-recommended-practice-document

entities.name: ChaoJi charging interface
entities.definition: Next-generation unified DC interface developed by China and Japan from the CHAdeMO 3.0 lineage, targeting 900 kW and above with backward compatibility through adapters.
entities.source: Driivz, EV charging standards and protocols — https://driivz.com/blog/ev-charging-standards-and-protocols

entities.name: IEC 62196 Type 2 (Mennekes)
entities.definition: Seven-pin AC connector used across Europe, supporting single- and three-phase charging up to 43.5 kW.

entities.name: SAE J1772
entities.name_zh: 北美交流充电接口 SAE J1772
entities.definition: North American AC charging connector and standard, rated up to 19.2 kW and also the AC half of CCS1.

entities.name: IEC 61851
entities.name_zh: IEC 61851 传导充电系统标准
entities.definition: International standard for conductive charging systems, defining charging modes 1 to 4 and the control pilot signalling used by AC charging.

entities.name: ISO 15118
entities.definition: International vehicle-to-charger communication standard covering Plug and Charge via certificates; part 15118-20 adds bidirectional power transfer for V2G and V2H.

entities.name: Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP)
entities.definition: Open protocol between charging stations and back-end management systems published by the Open Charge Alliance; it is independent of the vehicle-side plug standard.
entities.source: Open Charge Alliance / Driivz, EV charging standards and protocols — https://driivz.com/blog/ev-charging-standards-and-protocols

entities.name: Plug and Charge
entities.definition: Automatic authentication and billing at the start of a charging session using ISO 15118 certificate exchange, so no app or card is needed.

entities.name: AC Level 1 charging
entities.definition: Charging from a standard household outlet at around 120 V in North America, giving roughly 1.4-1.9 kW.
entities.source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center, charging levels — https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity_charging_home.html

entities.name: AC Level 2 charging
entities.definition: 208-240 V AC charging through a dedicated wallbox, typically 7-22 kW, corresponding to IEC 61851 mode 3.
entities.source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center, charging levels — https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity_charging_home.html

entities.name: 11 kW AC charging
entities.definition: Three-phase AC charging at 16 A per phase; the common European default onboard charger rating.
entities.source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center, charging levels — https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity_charging_home.html

entities.name: 22 kW AC charging
entities.definition: Three-phase AC charging at 32 A per phase; it requires a matching onboard charger and is limited by vehicle hardware, not the wallbox.
entities.source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center, charging levels — https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity_charging_home.html

entities.name: DC fast charging (DCFC)
entities.definition: Charging in which the off-board charger supplies DC directly to the pack, bypassing the onboard charger; typical public rates run from 50 kW to 400 kW and above.
entities.source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center, charging levels — https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity_charging_home.html

entities.name: High-power charging (HPC, 350 kW+)
entities.definition: CCS2-class public chargers rated 350-400 kW, used with 800 V vehicles to add roughly 250-300 km in about 15-20 minutes.
entities.source: Ionity / Driivz, EV charging standards and protocols — https://driivz.com/blog/ev-charging-standards-and-protocols

entities.name: 400 V architecture
entities.definition: Conventional EV pack and drivetrain voltage class around 350-450 V; DC charging current must rise steeply to exceed roughly 150-200 kW.

entities.name: 800 V high-voltage architecture
entities.definition: Doubling system voltage halves current for the same power, cutting cable and inverter losses and enabling sustained 250 kW+ charging with silicon carbide semiconductors.

entities.name: 4C fast charging
entities.definition: Charging at four times pack capacity, which corresponds to a full charge in about 15 minutes and requires a dedicated high-rate battery design.
entities.source: CATL official news, Super Technology Day / Naxtra Battery — https://www.catl.com/en/news/6401.html

entities.name: 5C fast charging
entities.definition: Charging at five times pack capacity; on a 5C-capable pack this yields roughly 10-80% in about ten minutes when paired with a high-power charger.
entities.source: CATL official news, Super Technology Day / Naxtra Battery — https://www.catl.com/en/news/6401.html

entities.name: Megawatt Charging System (MCS)
entities.definition: CharIN standard for heavy-duty vehicle charging targeting up to 3.75 MW at 1,250 V and 3,000 A.

entities.name: Battery swapping
entities.definition: Replenishment model in which the depleted pack is removed and a charged one installed, taking a few minutes and decoupling charging time from the vehicle.

entities.name: NIO Power Swap
entities.definition: NIO's automated battery swap stations, offered together with Battery-as-a-Service so customers lease the pack separately from the car.
entities.source: NIO official, Battery as a Service — https://www.nio.com/

entities.name: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G)
entities.definition: Exporting energy from an EV battery back to the public grid in exchange for payment; it requires a bidirectional vehicle, a bidirectional charger and a utility programme.

entities.name: Vehicle-to-load (V2L)
entities.definition: Powering external appliances from the traction battery through an outlet or adaptor, typically at 3.6 kW in Europe and up to 6 kW on some Chinese models.
entities.source: Mobility House, Which cars are V2G capable — https://mobilityhouse-energy.com/int_en/knowledge-center/article/which-cars-are-v2g-capable

entities.name: Vehicle-to-home (V2H)
entities.definition: Using the EV battery as a home backup or peak-shaving source through a bidirectional home charger.
entities.source: Mobility House, Which cars are V2G capable — https://mobilityhouse-energy.com/int_en/knowledge-center/article/which-cars-are-v2g-capable

entities.name: Bidirectional charging
entities.definition: Hardware and software that allow power to flow both into and out of the vehicle battery, enabling V2L, V2H and V2G use cases.

entities.name: Charging curve
entities.definition: Plot of charging power against state of charge. Power is highest at low SOC and tapers above roughly 80%, so the last 20% takes disproportionately long.
entities.source: Driivz, EV charging standards and protocols — https://driivz.com/blog/ev-charging-standards-and-protocols

entities.name: Onboard charger (OBC)
entities.definition: AC-to-DC converter built into the vehicle that sets the maximum AC charging rate, commonly 6.6-11 kW and up to 22 kW on three-phase models.
entities.source: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center, charging levels — https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/electricity_charging_home.html

entities.name: Tesla Supercharger
entities.definition: Tesla's proprietary DC fast charging network; V3 cabinets deliver 250 kW and V4 cabinets up to 500 kW with 1,000 V support.

entities.name: Permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM)
entities.definition: AC motor whose rotor uses permanent magnets, giving high power density and efficiency; the dominant traction motor in Chinese EVs.

entities.name: AC induction motor
entities.definition: Motor that induces rotor current instead of using permanent magnets; it is robust and can be freewheeled to cut drag when not needed.

entities.name: Wound-rotor synchronous motor (EESM)
entities.definition: Synchronous motor that creates the rotor field with a wound coil instead of permanent magnets, eliminating rare-earth materials at a small efficiency cost.
entities.source: ZF, I2SM electric motor / BMW 5th-generation eDrive — https://www.zf.com/

entities.name: Switched reluctance motor
entities.definition: Motor that produces torque purely from magnetic reluctance, with a simple iron rotor that needs no magnets or windings but requires advanced control to limit noise.

entities.name: e-axle (integrated electric drive unit)
entities.definition: Single assembly combining traction motor, inverter and reduction gearbox on one axle, which shortens high-voltage cabling and cuts weight and cost.

entities.name: Silicon carbide (SiC) power module
entities.definition: Wide-bandgap semiconductor used in inverters; it switches faster and tolerates higher temperatures than silicon, raising efficiency and enabling higher switching frequency.

entities.name: Insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT)
entities.definition: Silicon power switch used in traction inverters and onboard chargers, combining high input impedance with low conduction loss at moderate switching frequency.

entities.name: Dual-motor all-wheel drive
entities.definition: Configuration with one motor per axle, giving all-wheel traction and independent front/rear torque split without a mechanical propshaft.

entities.name: Tri-motor drivetrain
entities.definition: Three-motor layout, usually one front and two rear, used for high-performance models with rear torque vectoring.

entities.name: Quad-motor drivetrain
entities.definition: Four independent motors, one per wheel, enabling precise wheel-level torque control for off-road capability such as tank turns.
entities.source: Wikipedia, Yangwang U8 / BYD e4 platform — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangwang_U8

entities.name: Single-speed reduction gear
entities.definition: Fixed-ratio gearbox between motor and wheels used by most EVs, because the motor's wide speed range removes the need for multiple ratios.

entities.name: Two-speed transmission
entities.definition: Two-ratio gearbox used in some performance EVs so a short first gear improves launch and a long second gear raises top-speed efficiency.

entities.name: Regenerative braking
entities.definition: Recovering kinetic energy by running the traction motor as a generator during deceleration and storing the energy back in the battery.

entities.name: One-pedal driving
entities.definition: Driving mode in which strong regenerative braking is mapped to the accelerator pedal, so the brake pedal is rarely needed in normal traffic.

entities.name: Torque vectoring
entities.definition: Deliberately distributing drive torque left to right to rotate the car into a corner, which multi-motor EVs can do without a differential.

entities.name: In-wheel motor
entities.definition: Motor mounted inside the wheel hub, removing the drivetrain entirely but raising unsprung mass; used mainly in low-speed and specialist vehicles.

entities.name: Rare-earth-free motor
entities.definition: Traction motor designed without neodymium or dysprosium magnets, using wound-field or ferrite designs to avoid rare-earth supply risk.

entities.name: BYD DM-i super hybrid
entities.name_zh: 比亚迪 DM-i 超级混动
entities.definition: Plug-in hybrid system built around an electric hybrid architecture in which the engine mainly generates electricity, with a dedicated hybrid transmission for direct drive at high speed.
entities.source: BYD official, DM-i super hybrid — https://www.byd.com/

entities.name: Range-extender EV (EREV)
entities.definition: Series hybrid in which the combustion engine only drives a generator, so the wheels are always driven electrically; battery packs are typically larger than in a PHEV.

entities.name: Plug-in hybrid (PHEV)
entities.definition: Vehicle with both a combustion engine and a chargeable battery that can drive the wheels directly or electrically; Chinese policy treats long-range PHEVs as new-energy vehicles.

entities.name: Dedicated EV platform
entities.definition: Vehicle architecture designed around a skateboard battery floor from the outset, rather than adapted from a combustion platform, giving a flat floor and more interior space.

entities.name: Battery electric vehicle (BEV)
entities.definition: Vehicle propelled solely by an electric motor drawing energy from an onboard battery, with no combustion engine.

entities.name: Motor power density
entities.definition: Traction motor output per unit mass or volume, reported in kW/kg; higher values reduce drive-unit weight for a given output.

entities.name: Liquid cooling (battery)
entities.definition: Battery thermal management approach that circulates coolant through cold plates or channels to remove heat and equalise cell temperatures.
entities.source: Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering, CTB review (thermal management) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/mechanical-engineering/articles/10.3389/fmech.2026.1825484/full

entities.name: Direct refrigerant cooling
entities.definition: Design that routes refrigerant directly to a cold plate on the pack, removing the intermediate coolant loop for faster heat rejection.
entities.source: Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering, CTB review (thermal management) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/mechanical-engineering/articles/10.3389/fmech.2026.1825484/full

entities.name: Immersion cooling
entities.definition: Cooling in which cells are submerged in a dielectric fluid, giving very uniform temperature control and suppressing thermal propagation.

entities.name: Heat pump HVAC
entities.definition: Cabin heating system that moves heat with a refrigerant cycle instead of generating it resistively, saving substantial energy in cold weather.
entities.source: US DOE, Heat pumps for EV cabin heating / Wikipedia, Heat pump — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_pump

entities.name: CO2 (R744) heat pump
entities.definition: Heat pump using carbon dioxide as refrigerant; it keeps useful heating capacity at very low ambient temperature and has very low global warming potential.

entities.name: PTC heater
entities.definition: Positive-temperature-coefficient resistive heater used for cabin and battery heating; simple and effective but consumes significant energy.

entities.name: Battery preconditioning
entities.definition: Automatically bringing the pack to an optimal temperature before fast charging; cold packs otherwise charge far more slowly.

entities.name: Battery thermal management system (BTMS)
entities.definition: Combined hardware and control strategy that keeps cells within a target temperature window, balancing cooling, heating and temperature uniformity.
entities.source: Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering, CTB review — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/mechanical-engineering/articles/10.3389/fmech.2026.1825484/full

entities.name: Octovalve thermal manifold
entities.name_zh: 八通阀热管理集成模块
entities.definition: Multi-port valve that routes coolant between battery, drive units, cabin and heat pump from a single manifold, cutting the number of thermal loops and valves.
entities.source: Tesla, Model Y heat pump / Octovalve patent coverage — https://www.tesla.com/

entities.name: Phase change material (PCM)
entities.definition: Material that absorbs heat while melting at a set temperature, used to buffer cell temperature spikes and slow thermal propagation.

entities.name: Motor oil cooling
entities.definition: Spraying or circulating oil directly onto motor windings to remove heat; it raises continuous power density compared with water-jacket cooling.
entities.source: Wikipedia, Electric motor cooling / industry e-axle specifications — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_motor

entities.name: Thermal runaway propagation prevention
entities.definition: Pack-level design measures such as barriers, venting and spacing that stop one cell's thermal runaway from igniting its neighbours; China's GB 38031-2025 makes no-fire, no-explosion thermal propagation a mandatory requirement.
entities.source: Xinhua / China MIIT, GB 38031-2025 (thermal diffusion test) — https://www.news.cn/20260629/2a2fa1facc034e6ea24b73bcd582ab43/c.html

entities.name: R1234yf refrigerant
entities.definition: Low global-warming-potential HFO refrigerant that replaced R134a in most automotive air-conditioning systems.

entities.name: CLTC range standard
entities.name_zh: 中国 CLTC 续航工况
entities.definition: China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle defined in GB/T 38146.1-2019: a 30-minute, 14.48 km dynamometer cycle with low average speed and frequent stops, which usually reads more optimistic than real-world driving.
entities.source: Wikipedia, China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Light-Duty_Vehicle_Test_Cycle

entities.name: WLTP range standard
entities.name_zh: WLTP 全球统一测试规程
entities.definition: Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure, the lab cycle that replaced NEDC in Europe; its four-phase speed profile sits closer to real driving than NEDC.
entities.source: Wikipedia, Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide_Harmonised_Light_Vehicles_Test_Procedure

entities.name: NEDC range standard
entities.definition: New European Driving Cycle, a synthetic two-phase laboratory cycle replaced by WLTP in Europe from 2017-2019; its stable speed profile made range figures optimistic.

entities.name: EPA range rating
entities.definition: United States EPA rating derived from the UDDS urban and HWFET highway cycles with a 0.7 adjustment factor, making it the most conservative of the major range claims.

entities.name: Range standard conversion
entities.definition: Rules of thumb for translating one test cycle into another, such as CLTC multiplied by about 0.82 to approximate WLTP; they are estimates and should always carry the source standard.
entities.source: Wikipedia, China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle (cycle comparison table) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Light-Duty_Vehicle_Test_Cycle

entities.name: Real-world range
entities.definition: Distance actually achieved on the road, typically below every laboratory figure because of speed, gradient, load, climate control and temperature.
entities.source: Wikipedia, China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle (cycle comparison) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Light-Duty_Vehicle_Test_Cycle

entities.name: Winter range retention
entities.definition: Share of rated range available in sub-zero conditions; cabin heating and cold cell chemistry cut it sharply, and LFP packs lose more than NMC.

entities.name: Energy consumption (kWh/100 km)
entities.definition: Energy used per 100 km, the metric that links battery size to range and the fairest basis for comparing efficiency between models.
entities.source: Wikipedia, China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle (consumption comparison) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Light-Duty_Vehicle_Test_Cycle

entities.name: Range anxiety
entities.definition: Consumer concern about running out of charge before reaching a charger, a barrier to EV adoption that charger coverage and faster charging reduce.

entities.name: Usable versus gross battery capacity
entities.name_zh: 电池可用容量与标称容量
entities.definition: Difference between total installed capacity and the portion the BMS exposes to the driver; buffers protect the pack and mean some kWh are never usable.

entities.name: Highway range penalty
entities.definition: Additional energy per kilometre at steady high speed because aerodynamic drag grows with the square of velocity; low-speed cycles such as CLTC under-represent this effect.

entities.name: Integrated die-casting (gigacasting)
entities.definition: Casting large body sections such as a rear underbody as a single part using very high clamping-force presses, replacing dozens of welded stampings.

entities.name: Drag coefficient (Cd)
entities.definition: Dimensionless measure of how much aerodynamic drag a shape creates; combined with frontal area it defines CdA, which dominates highway energy use.

entities.name: Active grille shutter
entities.definition: Grille vanes that close at speed to cut cooling airflow drag and reopen when the drive system needs cooling.

entities.name: Flush door handle
entities.definition: Handle that stows flush with the door skin, removing a local separation bubble and reducing drag.

entities.name: Flat underbody panel
entities.definition: Smooth panelling under the car that prevents turbulent airflow underneath the battery, lowering drag and adding protection to the pack.

entities.name: Air suspension
entities.definition: Springing that uses air springs with adjustable pressure and height, letting the car lower itself at speed for aerodynamic benefit or raise itself over rough ground.

entities.name: Crumple zone
entities.definition: Deliberately deformable front or rear structure that absorbs crash energy over a controlled distance so the passenger cell stays intact.

entities.name: Hot-stamped ultra-high-strength steel
entities.definition: Steel press-formed while austenitic and quenched in the die, reaching tensile strengths around 1,500 MPa for lightweight passenger-cell reinforcement.

entities.name: Aluminium space frame
entities.definition: Body structure built from extruded and bonded aluminium sections rather than a monocoque of steel stampings, cutting weight at higher material cost.

entities.name: Torsional stiffness
entities.definition: Resistance of the body to twisting, measured in Nm/deg; structural battery designs such as CTB push values above 40,000 Nm/deg.
entities.source: ResearchInChina, Passenger Car CTP/CTC/CTB report (CTB structural contribution) — https://www.researchinchina.com/Htmls/Report/2024/73951.html

entities.name: IP68 battery pack sealing
entities.definition: Pack sealing rated dust-tight and protected against continuous immersion, the common rating for EV traction batteries.

entities.name: IP code
entities.definition: International two-digit ingress protection rating: the first digit covers solids and dust, the second covers water.

entities.name: C-NCAP
entities.name_zh: 中国新车评价规程 C-NCAP
entities.definition: Chinese new car assessment programme run by CATARC that scores crash protection and, in recent versions, active safety and battery safety for the domestic market.

entities.name: Euro NCAP
entities.name_zh: 欧洲新车安全评鉴 Euro NCAP
entities.definition: European new car assessment programme scoring adult and child occupant protection, vulnerable road user protection and safety assist systems.

entities.name: GB 38031 EV battery safety standard
entities.name_zh: 动力电池安全强制性国标 GB 38031
entities.definition: China's mandatory safety standard for traction batteries. The 2020 version required a five-minute warning before fire or explosion; the 2025 revision, published in March 2025, demands no fire and no explosion plus smoke that does not harm occupants, and adds bottom-impact and post-fast-charge short-circuit tests. It applies to newly type-approved models from 1 July 2026 and to already-approved models from 1 July 2027.
entities.source: China MIIT / Xinhua, GB 38031-2025 Electric vehicles traction battery safety requirements — https://www.news.cn/20260629/2a2fa1facc034e6ea24b73bcd582ab43/c.html
